analyst_view.overall: Early view: Córdoba are tenth under Iván Ania and strong at home (four wins in six), most recently 3-0 against Ceuta with two goals from Diego Percan. Las Palmas are 13th under Albert Sánchez, their third coach of the season, and their away games have been very open (24 goals in six).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean higher: Las Palmas' away games have averaged four goals and Córdoba's home games over three, and both defences have conceded more than 20.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Córdoba won 11 corners against Ceuta and attack wide at home, while Las Palmas won only four against Eldense, so most corners should go to Córdoba with a total near the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards. Córdoba had a second-yellow red and a violent-conduct ban after their game at Celta Fortuna, but only three yellows against Ceuta, so I stay with the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots. Córdoba took 14 against Ceuta and Las Palmas' open away games add volume, so the number looks fair.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, in line with my goals view: Córdoba had seven on target against Ceuta and Las Palmas concede plenty away.
